records.text: ENVIRONMENTAL SAFETY DURING THE PERIOD OF AUTHORISATION. 2026 Environmental Safety Case for the LLWR. LLWR/ESC/R(26)10179, May 2026.

Aerial discharge monitoring. There are currently two operational active ventilation systems on the LLWR site. Prior to discharge, all gaseous discharges pass through a double HEPA filtration system. The total activity in the gaseous discharges from the discharge stacks at the LLWR is very low. Figure 4.4: Annual discharges of total alpha and total beta activity to air from authorised discharge stacks.

Figure 4.5 presents the modelled flux of tritium-bearing water vapour to air from the present day to the end of the Period of Authorisation. The peak annual total flux of tritium calculated is 1.7 TBq, dominated by release from Vault 9, and it occurs in 2047.

Figure 4.7 presents the modelled flux to air for the duration of the Period of Authorisation. The rate of release is around 3 TBq y-1 for the majority of the period, dominated by releases from the trenches. The peak release of 3.4 TBq y-1 from across the whole site occurs in 2047.

Total annual doses from tritium in air are approximately 1 µSv or less and total annual doses from C-14 in air are less than 0.01 µSv. The release rate of radon is almost constant with time, with the peak dose of 6.2 µSv.
